label: verify-bm-buehler-materials-corpus

claims.claim: Corpus has no vat-photopolymer/powder-bed/Formlabs abstracts; printed-composite results traced to Objet Connex jetting (Dimas, Gu theses).
claims.note: The MIT DSpace thesis PDFs returned a Cloudflare/HTML page via curl and HTTP 429 via WebFetch; I did not re-run corpus_stats.py, so the counts are unchecked.

claims.claim: Transferable design logic includes ML-designed printed composite about 25x tougher than the stiff material, plus humidity-gated hysteretic stimulus.
claims.note: Gu thesis was blocked (two routes); the cited PMC6397028 (Liu et al., spider silk humidity torsion) contains no 'tougher' passage, so it does not carry the 25x quote.

claims.claim: Moduli 2187 and 0.53 MPa (ratio 4126) give Timoshenko coefficient 0.0058 at equal thickness, 0.4% of the 3/2 ceiling.
claims.note: I reproduced ratio 4126.4 and coefficient 0.00580 (0.0039 of 1.5, i.e. 0.39%) with the standard Timoshenko formula; the optimum ratio 64 and 41-44 figures and the thesis moduli were not checked (thesis unfetchable).

claims.claim: Flexible 80A Resin V2 data sheet reports +8% mass, +3% volume, -26 Shore A after 1 day in deionized water.
claims.note: Downloaded the Formlabs V2 TDS PDF and the row matches; the older-resin 0.7% comparison was not checked.

overall: One of four claims is supported (the Formlabs V2 water-immersion row, read from the data sheet). The arithmetic claim reproduces only in part. The two thesis-based claims could not be checked because MIT DSpace blocked every route. The 25x-tougher quote is also not in the PMC paper the agent cited, which is about spider silk.
